notes.text: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 54:11 together, up from 41% with Matheson.
Nick Suzuki returned in their last game after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 6% last season.
James Hagens is day to day (back injury), reported after he played in their last game.

stakes: The Canadiens go in second in the Atlantic with 23 points, 2 points behind the Bruins, first. A regulation win for the Canadiens would pull them level with the Bruins.

story.head: Pastrňák’s favorite opponent
paras: The Bruins have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh. The Canadiens (10-3-3) beat Utah 5-4 in overtime on Nov 5. Two of the league’s best teams meet. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Habs second (sixth in the NHL) and the Bruins first (tied for third). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Canadiens’ record (.719) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-4 in one-goal games. So is the Bruins’ (.735 on chances worth .562), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than anyone (1st) and take more penalties than they draw (32nd). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (28th), so the Bruins could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). Boston has allowed 2.35 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Canadiens’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Lane Hutson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring. Cole Caufield (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with a point in seven straight games against Boston. For the Bruins, David Pastrňák (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in eleven straight games against Montréal.

Jacob Fowler (7-1-1 / .925 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and will likely start. Boston has two options in net: Jeremy Swayman (8-3-1 / .912 SV% in 12 GS) and Michael DiPietro (4-1-0 / .924 SV% in 5 GS). Swayman has started six of their last ten games, but DiPietro got the last one on Nov 5. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.

The Bruins are newly without James Hagens.
Connor Clifton has missed the Bruins’ last three games.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
